title: Purple Heart Emoji 💜 Meaning: BTS, Loyalty and Glamour
description: The purple heart emoji 💜 means affection, admiration and loyalty, and for BTS fans it says “I purple you.” See what it means in texts, fandoms and military tributes.
summary: The 💜 purple heart emoji means warm affection with a note of admiration or loyalty. It is famous as the heart of BTS and their fans, who use it for “I purple you.” Elsewhere it shows friendship, family love, a liking for the color, or respect for military service.
meaning: In ordinary chats, 💜 is a friendly heart with a little flair. It is less romantic than red and less sunny than yellow, and people choose it for affection that feels tender or slightly glamorous. Purple has long been linked with royalty and luxury, so the emoji also turns up when someone is being treated like a queen, in birthday tributes, fashion posts and compliments about someone's style.

Its largest single community of users is the BTS fandom. The phrase “borahae,” usually translated “I purple you,” was coined by BTS member V, who explained purple as the last color of the rainbow and so a symbol of trusting and loving each other for a long time. ARMY adopted 💜 as the visual form of that promise. Under any BTS-related post, rows of purple hearts mean loyalty to the group and to fellow fans.

In the United States the name has an older meaning. The Purple Heart is a military decoration awarded to service members wounded or killed in action. The emoji is not a picture of the medal, but people use it on Memorial Day, Veterans Day and in tributes to honor recipients, often with a flag.

Purple is also the color of several awareness causes, including domestic violence and Alzheimer's campaigns, and of Spirit Day, when people wear purple to support LGBTQ youth against bullying. The heart marks those posts too. Finally there is simple color-matching: lavender fields, purple hair, grape soda and teams in purple such as the Lakers or Vikings.

contexts.label: In K-pop fandom
contexts.body: For ARMY, 💜 is identity. It appears in usernames, bios and nearly every comment directed at BTS or its members, and concert venues and landmarks have been lit purple to welcome the group. Fans of other acts generally avoid it for their own artists because the association is so strong. If a stranger online sends you a purple heart under BTS content, it is fandom solidarity.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: With friends and family it is a soft, affectionate sign-off. Mothers and grandmothers use it freely, and so do friends who find red too intense. It often reads as compassionate, which makes it a good heart for encouragement: “you were so brave today 💜.”

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: A purple heart is warm but not a clear romantic signal. It suggests fondness and maybe admiration. Some online guides claim it means lust or physical attraction, but that reading is not common in real conversations, and most senders are not thinking of it. Look at the words that come with it.

contexts.label: In tributes
contexts.body: Around US military holidays, 💜 honors wounded and fallen service members by reference to the Purple Heart medal. It also appears in memorial posts for Prince, whose signature color was purple, and for causes marked by purple ribbons. The wording of the post normally makes the reference plain.

examples.meaning: A tribute referring to the Purple Heart military decoration.
The heart matches the color of the photo.
Admiring compliment with a hint of glamour.
Support for LGBTQ youth and a stand against bullying.

combos.meaning: Enthusiastic love; in BTS spaces, a standard show of fan devotion.
Respect for Purple Heart recipients and wounded veterans.
Royal treatment or admiration for someone's elegance.
Team colors, most recognizably for Los Angeles Lakers fans.

confusedWith.difference: 💙 is cooler and plainer, signaling trust and steady friendship. 💜 is warmer and more expressive, with fandom and glamour associations. Their shades can look close on a dim screen, which matters when you are matching team or flag colors.
🩷 is cute and sweet, a light flirtation or girly accent. 💜 is a little deeper and more composed. Both are friendly, but pink is the likelier choice for crush territory.
🖤 is for dark humor, grief and gothic style. People building a moody palette often use both, but purple remains affectionate and sincere where black is edgy or mournful.

avoid: Do not use it to joke about the Purple Heart medal; many readers take the decoration very seriously.
Avoid assuming a sender is a BTS fan or is flirting; most purple hearts are just friendly.
If you want to state romantic love plainly, choose red.
design: A solid heart in a medium violet, the same shape as the red heart on each platform. Apple's version is a glossy, fairly bright purple, and others run from lilac toward a deeper grape. It dates from the original 2010 set, so it displays almost everywhere. The emoji is not modeled on the military medal, which is a gold-bordered heart bearing George Washington's profile.

faqs.a: It stands for “I purple you,” an expression coined by member V meaning to love and trust someone for a long time. Fans and the members exchange purple hearts as a sign of that bond, and purple has become the unofficial color of the fandom.

faqs.q: What does 💜 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: Typically affection for a friend, a fondness for purple, or fandom. If she is a BTS fan it may be her default heart. In flirtation it is a mild positive sign and not a declaration.

faqs.q: What does 💜 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: Usually friendly care or admiration. Guys send it less often than blue or red, so it may reflect a favorite team, a favorite color or copying the heart you sent first. It does not have a hidden meaning.

faqs.q: Does the purple heart emoji mean horny?
faqs.a: Some websites claim so, sometimes by linking it to the purple devil or eggplant emojis. In everyday use the heart itself is not read as sexual. If someone means that, the rest of the message will make it obvious.

faqs.q: Is the emoji the same as the Purple Heart medal?
faqs.a: No. The emoji is a plain purple heart from the original color set. The medal is a US military decoration for those wounded or killed in action. People borrow the emoji to refer to the medal because of the shared name.
